nodes.label: base-apps Kustomization (app list)
nodes.rationale: loki/mimir/tempo are deliberately excluded and managed by the dedicated wait:false monitoring Kustomization so their external Ceph-RGW S3 backend cannot block the base-apps -> apps dependency chain

nodes.label: cloudflare-tunnel IngressClass (external front door)
nodes.rationale: Cloudflare caps request bodies at 100MB, so registry pushes through the tunnel must use a chunked client (regctl); a plain docker push of a >100MB layer fails

nodes.label: dragonfly.dragonfly.svc.cluster.local:6379 (Redis replacement)
nodes.rationale: direct connection to the operator-managed master endpoint instead of Sentinel, so sentinelMasterSet stays empty; Harbor keeps DB indexes 0-7 with core pinned to 0

nodes.label: rook-ceph-rgw-feather-s3 (in-cluster Ceph RGW S3 endpoint)
nodes.rationale: the public s3.onelitefeather.net endpoint is unreachable from the registry pod and made every blob op time out with an s3aws 500, so the internal plain-HTTP RGW service is used

nodes.label: priorityClassName injection via HelmRelease postRenderer
nodes.rationale: charts that expose no priorityClassName value (bluemap, dependency-track, grafana) get it patched in post-render instead of forking the chart

nodes.label: otelcol.receiver.otlp default (grpc 4317 / http 4318)
nodes.rationale: single OTLP intake point reachable only over the internal step-ca-issued TLS network, not the public internet, so no auth layer is needed

nodes.label: otelcol.processor.transform strip_ansi_codes
nodes.rationale: CloudNet/Velocity/Paper console loggers emit 24-bit ANSI SGR color codes in the log body, unreadable once shipped as plain text to Loki; stripped before the severity filter

nodes.label: otelcol.processor.transform strip_verbose_resource_attrs
nodes.rationale: OTel's process resource detector adds command_line/command_args which for a JVM with agent + classpath flags exceeds Mimir's per-label-value length limit (err-mimir-label-value-too-long) on target_info; deleted before they become labels

nodes.label: otelcol.processor.filter drop_debug_logs
nodes.rationale: drops DEBUG/TRACE records using the OTLP severity_number the log4j2/logback appender already sets, avoiding text/regex matching; severity_number == 0 (unspecified) is kept rather than guessed at

nodes.label: HelmRelease dependency-track (chart =0.39.0)
nodes.rationale: api-server memory limit must stay >=5Gi (6Gi used) because Dependency-Track enforces a hard 4GB minimum JVM heap sized at ~80% of the limit; lowering it crashes the server

nodes.label: Ingress dependency-track-cloudflare-tunnel (path split /api,/health vs /)
nodes.rationale: mirrors the chart's ingress path split; the tunnel controller orders rules longest-path-first so /api and /health match before /

nodes.label: Azure AD OIDC login with user/team provisioning (Alpine OIDC)
HelmRelease grafana (2 replicas, HA unified alerting)
nodes.rationale: persistence disabled and state kept in Postgres so both replicas are interchangeable; unified alerting clusters over the headless service on :9094

nodes.label: Grafana datasource Loki (uid loki, TraceID derived field)
Grafana Discord contact point + discord.title/discord.message templates
Alert rule cnpg-backup-stale
nodes.rationale: cnpg_collector_last_available_backup_timestamp never updates for plugin-based (barman-cloud) backups and stays stuck at 0, so the rule reads cnpg_backup_stopped_at_seconds from kube-state-metrics customResourceState instead

nodes.label: Alert rule cnpg-backup-failing
nodes.rationale: failed Backup CRs never get a stoppedAt timestamp (only completed ones do), so the rule counts Backups with phase=failed whose createdAt falls inside the 24h staleness window

nodes.label: HelmRelease harbor (chart =1.19.1, v2.15.0 images)
nodes.rationale: expose.type=clusterIP with TLS disabled: the internal nginx does all path routing and TLS is terminated at Envoy or Cloudflare; maxIdleConns/maxOpenConns trimmed to 5/25 to cap Harbor's footprint on the shared CNPG Postgres

nodes.label: PodDisruptionBudget harbor-registry (minAvailable 1)
nodes.rationale: the registry runs as a single replica because chunked uploads are session-bound to one pod; minAvailable:1 keeps it up across voluntary disruptions so node drains need a deliberate cordon/force

nodes.label: PodDisruptionBudget harbor-nginx
nodes.rationale: nginx is the single front service all Harbor traffic funnels through; keeping one pod up across node drains avoids 504 Gateway Timeouts

nodes.label: Secret harbor-secret (admin pw, S3 keys, DB pw, Redis pw)
Harbor single-replica registry (session-bound chunked blob uploads)
nodes.rationale: with >1 replica the chunk PATCH can land on a pod that does not know the upload session started by the POST, producing intermittent 'failed to send blob (chunk) ... 404'

hyperedges.label: Single OTLP intake point fanning traces/metrics/logs to Tempo, Mimir and Loki
Harbor dual front door: internal Envoy HTTPRoute + external Cloudflare tunnel Ingress onto one clusterIP nginx
Grafana LGTM correlation: Loki TraceID derived field -> Tempo -> Mimir service map/metrics
